questions.q: In "Know your customer and market Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: In language schools: Test learner level and goal: work, study, travel, exams.
Map the process from first contact to paid and closed. Typical stages: enquiry, quote, preparation, delivery of the learner, check, payment, follow-up.
Set service rules for answering customers: reply times, tone, how to apologise and fix.
Test the plan: what if sales fall by a quarter, or cost rises by a tenth?

questions.q: In "Rules, registration and data duties in Brazil Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Count the market in units: how many learners could one area buy in a month? Use two public sources and your own count, then take the lower figure.
In language schools: Train teachers in feedback and error correction.
Check that insurance and legal duties match the risk you actually carry.
Consumer law gives buyers clear rights on information, returns and complaints. Put your terms in plain Portuguese.

questions.q: In "Design the offer Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Find the sector rules for language schools: licences, inspections, professional registers. List each with the office that issues it and the renewal date.
Make a 12-month cash plan. Cash timing matters as much as profit: customers may pay late, suppliers may want money first.
Name the key resource at each stage: a placed level and a plan. Note what happens if it is missing.
Add one proof for each promise: a sample, a test result, a guarantee or a customer record.

o: Map the process from first contact to paid and closed. Typical stages: enquiry, quote, preparation, delivery of the learner, check, payment, follow-up.
Break-even units = fixed cost divided by contribution. Plan to pass it by a safe margin.
Consumer law gives buyers clear rights on information, returns and complaints. Put your terms in plain Portuguese.
Check that insurance and legal duties match the risk you actually carry.

questions.q: In "Safety, quality and risk Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Write who does what in an emergency, and rehearse it once a quarter.
In language schools: Know cost per class hour and seats filled.
Name the key resource at each stage: a placed level and a plan. Note what happens if it is missing.
Describe the core offer in three lines: what is delivered (a taught language course), the standard it meets, and the time it takes.

questions.q: In "People, skills and service Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Write who does what in an emergency, and rehearse it once a quarter.
For the top five, choose a control: remove the hazard, replace it, guard it, train people, or use protective gear, in that order of preference.
Fix the cause of a defect, not the symptom. Ask 'why' five times and record the answer.
Train by showing, doing with support, then doing alone with a check. Record sign-off per task.

questions.q: In "Money: cost, price and break-even Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Test the plan: what if sales fall by a quarter, or cost rises by a tenth?
Choose three measures: speed, quality (errors per 100) and customer rating. Review them every week.
Personal data of customers falls under Brazil's data protection law (LGPD). Collect only what you need, say why, keep it safe, and name who answers questions.
In language schools: Grow with levelled groups and exam preparation.

questions.q: In "Grow, measure and renew Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Set one measurable target for 90 days, such as 'raise repeat customers from 20% to 30%'.
In language schools: Train teachers in feedback and error correction.
Write a role card for each person: purpose, five tasks, the standard for each, and who to ask for help.
Count the market in units: how many learners could one area buy in a month? Use two public sources and your own count, then take the lower figure.
